We need to find d³ - (1/d³)

questions.question: Two cards are drawn successively without replacement from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability of drawing two aces is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Probability of the first card being an ace = 4/52 = 1/13.

Since the first card is not replaced, remaining cards = 51 and remaining aces = 3.

Probability of the second card being an ace = 3/51 = 1/17.

Total probability = (1/13) × (1/17) = 1/221.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/221.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of cards in a well-shuffled pack = 52

Total number of aces in the pack = 4

Number of cards drawn successively without replacement = 2

**Formula Used:**

Probability = Number of Favorable Outcomes ÷ Total Number of Possible Outcomes

Number of ways to choose r items from n items = ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ [r! × (n − r)!]

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total ways to draw 2 cards from 52 cards = ⁵²C₂

⇒ ⁵²C₂ = (52 × 51) ÷ (2 × 1) = 26 × 51 = 1326

⇒ Favorable ways to draw 2 aces from 4 aces = ⁴C₂

⇒ ⁴C₂ = (4 × 3) ÷ (2 × 1) = 2 × 3 = 6

⇒ Probability of drawing two aces = Favorable ways ÷ Total ways

⇒ Probability = 6 ÷ 1326

⇒ Probability = 1/221

**∴ The correct answer is 1/221.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Independent Events (With Replacement)

If the first card is replaced before drawing the second, the events are independent. The probability formula is P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).

Dependent Events (Without Replacement)

If the card is not replaced, the second draw depends on the first draw's outcome. The formula is P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B|A).

questions.question: Identify a structure found in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.

• Mesosomes are invaginated structures found in prokaryotic cells, particularly in bacteria.

• Mesosomes are involved in various cellular processes such as cell wall formation during cell division, DNA replication, and distribution to daughter cells.
 
• These structures are also associated with increasing the surface area of the plasma membrane for enzymatic activities.

• Plastids are double-membrane organelles found in the cells of plants and algae.
 
• They are involved in the synthesis and storage of food, most notably photosynthesis in chloroplasts.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm**
 
 
• The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance within the cell membrane, excluding the nucleus.
 
• It houses various organelles and is the site for most cellular processes.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes.
 
• They break down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
 
 
• **Mesosomes in Detail**
 
 
• Mesosomes were once thought to be artifacts of cell preparation but are now considered functional structures.
 
• They play a role in the respiratory processes of the cell by hosting enzymes involved in cellular respiration.

questions.question: The concept of "judicial review" in India allows the judiciary to review and strike down laws that are found to be:

options.text: Supported by a two-thirds majority in the State Legislature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** In violation of fundamental rights**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **"judicial review"** in India allows the judiciary (mainly the Supreme Court and High Courts) to review laws and executive actions to ensure that they comply with the **Constitution of India**.
 
• If a law is found to violate the **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed under the Constitution or go beyond the constitutional provisions,
 
 
• the judiciary can declare it unconstitutional or invalid.
 
 
 
• It primarily focuses on protecting the **Fundamental Rights** of citizens and upholding the **Constitutional structure**.
 
• Judicial review can strike down any law that violates fundamental rights,
 
 
• even if it has been passed by Parliament or supported by the President or a majority in the legislature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of judicial review in India has been borrowed from the **United States Constitution**.
 
• In the landmark case of **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**, the U.S. Supreme Court, under Chief Justice John Marshall,
 
 
• established the principle of judicial review, allowing the courts to invalidate laws that were contrary to the U.S. Constitution.
 
 
 
• This principle was incorporated into the Indian legal system during the framing of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions has/have the power to issue a writ of 'Habeas corpus' as per the Constitution of India?

options.text: The Supreme Court and the High Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __The Supreme Court and the High Court.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Habeas corpus is the Latin term which means ‘you must have the body’.
 
• It is the order issued by the court to present the detenu before the court and to check whether the arrest was lawful or not.
 
• The supreme court under Article 32 and the high court under Article 226 have the power to issue writs of 'Habeas corpus'.
 
• Though under Article 32 the supreme courts issue the writs if there is any violation of the fundamental rights of a person but the High Court under Article 226 has a wider jurisdiction to issue the writ for both a violation of the legal as well as the fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The concept of the writs is to enable the immediate determination of the rights of an individual and help the person to achieve the benefit of his right.
 
• There are five types of writs in our constitution those are as follows:
 
 
• Writ of habeas corpus
 
• Writ of Mandamus
 
• Writ of prohibition
 
• Writ of certiorari
 
• Writ of quo warranto
 
 
 
• The writ of mandamus is the order or command issued by any statute or any authority sanctioned by law to any person, corporation or any other authority in order to perform any public duty.
 
• The writ of prohibition means is a writ issued by the higher authority to its subordinate authority in order to stop something which the law prohibits.
 
• This writ can only be issued against a judicial and quasi-judicial body.
 
• The term certiorari is a Latin word that means to be informed.
 
• This writ is issued by the higher court to review the actions of the lower court.
 
• Writ of quo warranto means by what authority.
 
• This writ is issued which requires a person to show by what authority he has exercised his powers or rights.

questions.question:
Ocean Currents occur in Oceans and Seas due to which of the following?

1. Atmospheric circulation on the earth

2. Influence of insolation

3. Temperature difference and salinity difference

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Ocean Currents:**

 
• Ocean currents are the** most important ocean movements because of their influence on the climatology of various regions**. 
 
• Ocean currents are like river flow in oceans.
 
• They represent a regular volume of water in a definite path and direction.

**Forces Responsible for Ocean Currents:**

 
• **Influence of insolation:**

 
 
• **Heating by solar energy causes the water to expand.**
 
• That is why, **near the equator, the ocean water is about 8 cm higher** in level than in the middle latitudes.
 
• This causes a **very slight gradient** and water tends to flow down the slope.
 
• The **flow is normally from east to west.***** Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Influence of wind (atmospheric circulation):**
 
 
• Wind blowing on the surface of the ocean pushes the water to move.
 
• **Friction between the wind and the water's surface** affects the movement of the water body in its course.
 
• The **oceanic circulation pattern roughly corresponds to the earth’s atmospheric circulation pattern.**
 
• The air circulation over the oceans in the **middle latitudes is mainly anticyclonic** [Sub-tropical High-Pressure Belt] (more pronounced in the southern hemisphere than in the northern hemisphere due to differences in the extent of landmass). *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• Temperature difference and Salinity difference:
 
 
• The temperature difference and salinity difference are the secondary forces.
 
• Differences in water density affect the vertical mobility of ocean currents (vertical currents).
 
• Water with high salinity is denser than water with low salinity and in the same way cold water is denser than warm water.
 
• Denser water tends to sink, while relatively lighter water tends to rise.
 
• **Cold-water ocean currents** occur when the cold water at the poles sinks and slowly moves towards the equator.
 
• **Warm-water currents** travel out from the equator along the surface, **flowing towards the poles to replace the sinking cold water**. * Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Influence of gravity:**
 
 
• **Gravity tends to pull the water down** to pile and create gradient variation.
 
 
 
• **Influence of Coriolis force:**
 
 
• The **Coriolis force intervenes and causes the water to move to the right in the northern hemisphere** and to the left in the southern hemisphere.
 
• These** large accumulations of water** and the flow around them are called **Gyres**.
 
• These produce large circular currents in all the ocean basins. One such circular current is the **Sargasso Sea.**

• Khyal is a major form of Hindustani classical music in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Its name comes from a Persian/Arabic word meaning imagination.

questions.question: In which order did Mendeleev arrange the elements in his periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increasing atomic mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the elements in his periodic table based on their **increasing atomic mass**.
 
• He grouped elements with similar chemical properties into vertical columns called **groups**.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table to **predict the existence of undiscovered elements** and their properties.
 
• The periodic table was published in **1869**, marking a significant advancement in the study of chemistry.
 
• Although atomic mass was the primary criterion, Mendeleev occasionally altered the arrangement to ensure elements with similar properties were aligned correctly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table:**

 
 
• A tabular arrangement of chemical elements organized by their **atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties**.
 
• The modern periodic table is based on the **Moseley’s concept of increasing atomic number**, rather than atomic mass.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• The total mass of protons and neutrons in an atom's nucleus.
 
• Mendeleev used atomic mass as a criterion because atomic numbers were unknown at the time.
 
 
 
• **Predictions Made by Mendeleev:**
 
 
• Mendeleev successfully predicted the properties of elements like **gallium (eka-aluminum)** and **germanium (eka-silicon)**.
 
• These predictions were later confirmed with the discovery of these elements.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Mendeleev’s Table:**
 
 
• Some elements were placed out of order based on atomic mass to align with chemical properties.
 
• The periodic table did not account for the existence of **isotopes**, which have the same atomic number but different atomic masses.

questions.question: The 73rd Amendment of the Constitution enables the states with a population of less than 20 lakhs to have a minimum ______ structure in the local governance of the state.

__
 
• The **73rd Amendment of the Constitution** was passed in **1992 **to provide constitutional status to the** Panchayati Raj Institutions **(PRIs) and to strengthen the** local self-governance** in rural areas of India.
 
• The Amendment provides for a** three-tier structure** of local governance in states with a population of** more than 20 lakhs**, while states with a population of **less than 20 lakhs** can have a minimum **two-tier structure.**

• The purpose of the Amendment is to empower the **local communities** and to ensure their participation in **decision-making, planning and implementation** of developmental programs.
 
• **Union rule,** on the other hand, refers to the** central government's control **over the state governments, which is not related to the local governance structure.
